findings.quote: Most genes lie on chromosomes that are not sex chromosomes, and they come as a pair, one allele from each parent.
findings.problem: Boundary test fails. The round-5 rewording moved 'Most' onto where genes lie, so 'they come as a pair, one allele from each parent' is now stated without a limit (the round-4 text said 'Most genes on non-sex chromosomes come as a pair'). It fails for a polyploid, which the lesson itself teaches: 'A polyploid has extra whole sets of chromosomes', and Example #7's plant with a doubled chromosome set carries four copies of each gene, not a pair. It also fails for a diploid made by asexual reproduction, which the lesson says has one parent. The next sentence excepts only haploid organisms. Example #1 step 1 repeats the same unlimited rule as a reason ('This gene is on a non-sex chromosome, so each individual has two copies'), a fact the stem never gives and that holds only for a diploid organism.
findings.source: Checklist B01; reader rules, Added after the Sol audit (test each general statement against a known exception); the lesson's own Sympatric Speciation paragraph and Example #7; OpenStax Biology 2e, 18.2 (polyploidy)

findings.quote: A change gained in a lifetime, such as larger muscles from exercise, does not change the alleles that parents pass on.
findings.problem: Boundary test fails against the lesson's own exception. The sentence says any change gained in a lifetime leaves the passed-on alleles unchanged. A mutation that arises during life in the cells that make gametes is a change gained in a lifetime that does change the alleles passed on, and the lesson's Trap #4 says exactly this: 'changes gained during life are not passed on. A mutation in the DNA that offspring receive is the exception.' The Mutation section says the same. Example #3 and Trap #4 now give the student two different rules. The base hedged the sentence ('Many changes acquired during an individual's lifetime ... do not alter the inherited DNA variants'); the rewrite dropped the hedge. Earlier rounds did not raise it.
findings.source: Checklist B01; reader rules, Added after the Sol audit; the lesson's own Mutation section and Trap #4; base 7032eec5 Example #2 step 2

findings.quote: This concept is used mainly for organisms that reproduce sexually.
findings.problem: This species paragraph now has six sentences, over the one-to-three limit; the round-5 fix added the fertile and sterile sentences to it. Other paragraphs with four sentences: the Comparing the Four Causes paragraph, the allopatric speciation paragraph (the fix merged two paragraphs), the sympatric speciation paragraph, and the first Exam Strategies paragraph (the fix added a sentence). The round-4 instance, the Exam Strategies cue paragraph, is fixed.
